newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent rebounds slightly after overnight fall.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent rebounds slightly after overnight fall.

text.p: SIMEX Brent crude futures rebounded marginally late afternoon on Thursday on short covering as well as technicals, brokers said.
They said the market has been oversold this week after initial bullish sentiment over the Iran-Europe tension fizzled off followed by the bearish American Petroleum Institute crude data.
Brokers also said the market failed to follow through on the overnight fall in crude values amid the soft concerns over soft U.S. gasoline demand.

June last traded at $17.82 per barrel, up three cents from London's $17.81-close on Wednesday, after recording 166 lots. July last traded at $18.04 per barrel, up four cents after registering 12 lots.
Brokers said support is seen at $17.50/$17.75 with resistance at $18.35.
But NYMEX crude on ACCESS remained soft on bearish fundamentals, to last trade at $19.33, down two cents from its last official close.
